shared_elements: carved low relief on a large rough stone monument/boulder
upper rectangular register resembling a headdress or crown with vertical/horizontal bar elements
horizontal banded elements across the lower portion
weathered, pitted stone surface with eroded detail
justification: Both are monolithic stones bearing shallow relief organised in the same vertical sequence: a boxy headdress-like register at the top with bar and vertical elements, a large curvilinear central motif with scrolls and a disc below it, and horizontal bands sweeping across the lower field. The clearest difference is legibility and framing: B's central motif reads as a distinct profile creature head with a well-defined eye and volute, while A's central design is more abstract and dispersed, and the two are shown in wholly different contexts (lit museum display versus a half-buried outdoor block in monochrome), which makes surface tone and detail hard to compare directly.
